vignette: Kamran's life was forever changed on a sweltering summer evening when a devastating earthquake struck his hometown. He was at home with his wife and two young children, huddled together in their small apartment as the walls cracked and furniture crashed to the floor. The sounds of shattering glass, crumbling concrete, and screams from neighboring buildings still echo in his mind like a cacophony of terror. As he frantically tried to shield his family from falling debris, Kamran's thoughts were consumed by a desperate desire to protect them at all costs. In the weeks that followed, Kamran struggled to make sense of the disaster. He found himself fixating on what could have been done differently, replaying scenarios in which he might have saved more lives or minimized the destruction. His mind became preoccupied with thoughts of revenge against an invisible enemy – the earthquake itself, as if it were a sentient force that had deliberately targeted his community. This rumination served as a coping mechanism, allowing him to temporarily distract himself from feelings of helplessness and survivor's guilt. Kamran began to avoid hospitals, ambulances, and physical examinations, fearing they would remind him of the horrors he witnessed during the earthquake. Even routine check-ups for his children made him anxious, transporting him back to that fateful day when medical personnel were overwhelmed by the sheer number of injured victims. He started forcing himself to focus only on positive thoughts – a deliberate attempt to counterbalance the darkness that lurked within. However, this effort was constantly disrupted by Kamran's heightened sensitivity to his surroundings. Unexpected movements nearby would send him into high alert, as if danger could strike at any moment. He began to meticulously survey new environments, mentally mapping escape routes and exits before feeling secure enough to relax. Even gentle touches from loved ones made him flinch, a startle response that was both instinctual and disorienting. As memories of the earthquake resurfaced, Kamran would experience them with unrelenting vividness – sights, sounds, smells, and sensations blurring together in an agonizing reenactment. He would hear the anguished cries for help, feel the suffocating dust coating his lungs, and see the shattered remnants of what once was. The sequence of events remained jumbled in his mind, fragmented recollections refusing to coalesce into a coherent narrative. Kamran couldn't shake off the feeling that he had somehow failed – that someone else would have better navigated this disaster. Self-doubt gnawed at him, as if his actions on that fateful day were a personal failing rather than an unavoidable circumstance. This self-blame merged with a growing despair; Kamran was convinced that nothing good could happen to him anymore, that happiness had been extinguished forever. As the months dragged on, these ruminations and fears insidiously crept into Kamran's daily life. His performance at work suffered as he found himself increasingly preoccupied by potential threats – what if a fire broke out in the office? What if an earthquake struck while he was commuting? His colleagues began to notice his distraction, and his relationships with them grew strained. Kamran's wife, Nasrin, too, struggled to connect with her husband. She noticed that he had become withdrawn, avoiding family gatherings or public events, fearing they might trigger another episode of anguish. Their children began to sense their father's unease, tiptoeing around him as if afraid to disturb a fragile balance. Kamran finally realized that his efforts to cope were no longer working – that the very mechanisms he had relied upon to manage his emotions were now suffocating him. He knew he needed help, not just for himself but for those who loved and depended on him. It was with trepidation and a glimmer of hope that Kamran scheduled an appointment with a therapist, praying that together they might unravel the tangled threads of his trauma and guide him toward healing.
